SUMMARY

The two domains were unrelated in SCOPe 2.04 and are now sister families inside one superfamily. In 2.04 they shared nothing below class b (All beta proteins); in current SCOPe (2.08, released 2021-09-22, latest periodic update 2026-08-16) they sit in the same fold and the same superfamily, so SCOPe now asserts their common ancestry while keeping them in separate families. The reclassification moved the collagenase domain, not the toxin domain.

1. WHAT CHANGED, EXACTLY

ColG collagen-binding domain (CBD 3B) in 1nqd, a 1.65 A calcium-bound structure of the Clostridium histolyticum class I collagenase ColG C-terminal module:

- SCOPe 2.04 lineage of d1nqda_ (sunid 86025): b -> b.23 CUB-like -> b.23.2 Collagen-binding domain (superfamily) -> b.23.2.1 Collagen-binding domain (family) -> Class 1 collagenase -> Clostridium histolyticum [TaxId 1498]. Chain B was a single whole-chain domain d1nqdb_ (sunid 86026), also b.23.2.1.
- Current SCOPe 2.08 lineage of d1nqda_ (same sunid 86025): b -> b.18 Galactose-binding domain-like (fold) -> b.18.1 Galactose-binding domain-like (superfamily) -> b.18.1.36 Collagen-binding domain (family) -> Class 1 collagenase -> Clostridium histolyticum [TaxId 1498].

Cry3A C-terminal domain (domain III) in 1dlc, the 2.5 A Bacillus thuringiensis insecticidal delta-endotoxin structure:

- d1dlca1 = 1dlc A:500-644, sccs b.18.1.3, family delta-Endotoxin, C-terminal domain, species Bacillus thuringiensis tenebrionis CRYIIIA (BT13) [TaxId 1444]. This is identical in 2.04 and 2.08 (same sunid 23719, same sccs, same residue range). The toxin domain did not move.

So the change is one-sided. Before: different folds, b.23 versus b.18, i.e. no homology claim at all. After: one superfamily, b.18.1, two families, b.18.1.36 versus b.18.1.3, i.e. a remote-homology claim with no family-level (close) relationship. SCOPe's own homology endpoint reports homology_implied_by_level = true with homology_scope "sf" for b.18.1, and homology_scope "fa" for each family, which is the formal statement that common ancestry is asserted at superfamily strength only.

Supporting structural changes to the hierarchy: superfamily b.23.2 no longer exists in 2.08 (the node 404s in that release). Fold b.23 CUB-like survives but now contains only b.23.1 Spermadhesin CUB domain, b.23.3 Acetamidase/Formamidase-like and b.23.4 Complement system CUB domain. Superfamily b.18.1 grew from 33 families in 2.04 to 35 in 2.08, the two additions being b.18.1.36 Collagen-binding domain and b.18.1.37 Clostridium perfringens enterotoxin (CPE), C-terminal domain. Both new families are clostridial and were added together, which is the signature of a single curatorial decision rather than two independent moves.

2. WHEN IT HAPPENED

The move landed in SCOPe 2.05, not later. d1nqda_ already carries sccs b.18.1.36 in 2.05 (freeze 2014-12-23, release 2015-02-05), 2.06 and 2.07, and b.18.1.36 does not resolve at all in 2.04. The assignment has therefore been stable for four releases and through the 2.08 periodic updates up to 2026-08-16. Anyone comparing "2.04 versus current" is really seeing a 2.05 revision.

3. EVIDENCE FOR COMMON ANCESTRY

(a) Curator-cited literature, the decisive evidence. The family node b.18.1.36 carries the comment "PubMed 17977833 describes likely homology between (linkscop: d2quoa_), (linkscop: d1w99a3), and (linkscop: d1nqdb_)", with PubMed 17977833 as the only cross-reference on the node. Read carefully, the cited chain of homology is: ColG CBD (d1nqdb_) to the Cry4Ba delta-endotoxin C-terminal domain (d1w99a3, sccs b.18.1.3) to the Clostridium perfringens enterotoxin C-terminal domain (d2quoa_, sccs b.18.1.37). Two precision points follow. First, the published link runs through Cry4Ba, not Cry3A: 1dlc's d1dlca1 is never named in the SCOPe comment. Cry3A domain III inherits the relationship only because it belongs to the same family b.18.1.3 as d1w99a3, so the 1nqd-to-1dlc statement is a transitive inference across one family node, not a directly published pairwise alignment. Second, the comment cites the obsolete identifier d1nqdb_, which no longer resolves in 2.08; the curatorial note is stale with respect to current domain identifiers even though the classification itself is current.

(b) Topology and fold description. SCOPe describes b.18 Galactose-binding domain-like as "sandwich; 9 strands in 2 sheets; jelly-roll" and b.23 CUB-like as "sandwich, 10 strands in 2 sheets; jelly-roll". Both parent folds are jelly-roll beta sandwiches, which explains both the original 2.04 placement and why the correction is subtle rather than obvious: the discriminating feature is strand count and sheet topology, not overall architecture. The 1nqd PDB keywords themselves say "beta sandwich, metalloprotease, collagen-binding domain, calcium". The reassignment is a judgement that ColG CBD's strand topology matches the 9-stranded lectin-like galactose-binding/discoidin sandwich rather than the 10-stranded CUB sandwich.

(c) Structure-comparison evidence from SCOPe's own FATCAT-based neighbour lists. Querying chain 1nqdA returns an empty structure-hit list under the default filters (p <= 0.05, initial RMSD < 4), and the domain-level fatcat-chain-statistics for sunid 86025 returns status "not_applicable" with no supporting hits at the minimum of two. The informative list is for 1nqjA, the sequence-cluster representative of 1nqdA (99.16 percent identity over 119 alignment columns, Smith-Waterman). Its significant hits spread across the galactose-binding superfamily: d2quoa_ CPE C-terminal domain b.18.1.37 at p = 1.4e-06 and 10.26 percent identity; d2xh6a2 b.18.1.0 Clostridium perfringens automated match at p = 1.93e-06; d1wmfa1 alkaline serine protease KP-43 C-terminal domain b.18.1.20 at p = 2e-06; d1ux7a_ endo-1,4-beta-xylanase D b.18.1.28 at p = 1.32e-03; d2xhna3 b.18.1.0 at p = 2.17e-03. Independently, chain 1dlcA (its own cluster representative) hits d1w99a3 Cry4Ba delta-endotoxin C-terminal domain b.18.1.3 at p = 2e-04, d1ux7a_ b.18.1.28 at p = 7.46e-03 and d1w9wa_ CBM6 b.18.1.10 at p = 7.6e-03. Both domains therefore reach independently into b.18.1 at single-digit-to-low-double-digit sequence identity, and they share at least one common structural neighbour, xylanase D d1ux7a_. Crucially, neither hit list contains the other domain directly, so the structural support for the specific 1nqd-to-1dlc pair is transitive through superfamily members and not a direct pairwise FATCAT match. Residual CUB-like similarity persists too: 1nqjA still hits d3dema1 b.23.1.0 at p = 1.28e-03, which is why the original placement was defensible.

(d) Family membership consistency. Family b.18.1.36 now holds ten domains from five entries, all Clostridium histolyticum class I collagenase CBDs: d1nqda_, d1nqdb1, d1nqja_, d1nqjb_, d4hpka_, d4hpkb_, d2o8oa_, d2o8ob2, and the tandem pair d5ikua1 (A:773-890) and d5ikua2 (A:891-1008). Family b.18.1.3 holds the delta-endotoxin C-terminal domains including d1dlca1 and d1w99a3, and carries the comment "automatically mapped to Pfam 03944" with xref PF03944. The collagen-binding family has no Pfam cross-reference in 2.08, so sequence-profile corroboration is one-sided.

4. FUNCTIONAL EVIDENCE AND WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE

The shared functional logic is architectural, not mechanistic. Both domains are C-terminal accessory binding modules appended to a secreted multidomain bacterial virulence protein, each presenting a shallow face of a jelly-roll beta sandwich to a macromolecular target, and both sit in a superfamily dominated by targeting and ligand-binding modules: galactose-binding domain, discoidin/FA58C, CBM6, CBM15, CBM22, APC10-like, ephrin receptor ligand-binding domain, beta-galactosidase/glucuronidase N-terminal domain, XRCC1 N-terminal domain, KP-43 protease C-terminal domain. ColG CBD is the collagen-targeting module of the collagenase and is calcium dependent: 1nqd is the calcium-complexed form (domain comment "complexed with ca"), and the 2.04 superfamily annotation recorded that the "N-terminal strand appears only in calcium-free form". Cry3A domain III is the lectin-like C-terminal domain implicated in receptor and carbohydrate recognition and in specificity. Convergence on "substrate-adhesion module bolted onto a secreted toxin or enzyme" is consistent with descent from a common ligand-binding ancestor.

Unsafe transfers to avoid:

- Do not transfer binding specificity. The same scaffold in b.18.1 binds galactose, xylan, cellulose, ephrin, collagen and ubiquitin-ligase substrates. Superfamily membership says nothing about ligand. It is not supported to infer that Cry3A domain III binds collagen, nor that ColG CBD binds insect midgut receptors.
- Do not transfer catalytic or toxic function. Neither domain carries any activity. ColG's peptidase activity lies in its N-terminal M9B catalytic domain, which is absent from 1nqd entirely (the entry is only the isolated CBD 3B). Cry3A's membrane-perforating activity lies in domain I, classified separately as d1dlca3, sccs f.1.3.1, class f Membrane and cell surface proteins; 1dlc's middle lectin domain is d1dlca2 at b.77.2.1. So the homology statement touches only the accessory modules of both proteins and carries no implication about collagenolysis or insecticidal pore formation.
- Do not read family-level similarity into a superfamily-level claim. b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3 are distinct families precisely because sequence identity (about 10 to 26 percent in the relevant FATCAT comparisons) and functional divergence rule out a close relationship. SCOPe's homology_scope is "sf", not "fa".
- Do not treat the 2.04 and 2.08 records as interchangeable. Any pipeline keyed on sccs b.23.2.1 or on the domain identifier d1nqdb_ breaks silently against current SCOPe; a pipeline keyed on sunid 86025 still resolves but now means something different. Note also that sunid 86026 denoted whole-chain d1nqdb_ in 2.04 and denotes d1nqdb1 (B:893-1008) in 2.08, with residues B:891-892 split off as d1nqdb2 at l.1.1.1 (class l, artifacts). Domain boundaries were refined at the same time as the fold reassignment.

5. TEMPLATE AND REPRESENTATIVE CAVEATS

- 1nqd is the calcium-bound CBD; 1nqj is the related form and is the ASTRAL sequence-cluster representative for chain A. SCOPe's API explicitly warns that matches, coordinates and classifications of a representative must not be attributed directly to the requested chain, and the calcium-dependent N-terminal strand difference is a concrete reason that matters here. The structural evidence quoted above for ColG is representative-derived.
- Family b.18.1.36 mixes manual and automated assignments: d5ikua1 is an "automated match to d1nqda_". Choosing it as a modelling template inherits a propagated rather than curated classification.
- 1dlc is a 1994 deposition at 2.5 A with the SCOPe-selected PDB revision dated 2009-02-24, so it is a moderate-resolution template; Cry4Ba d1w99a3 is the family member actually used in the published homology argument.
- For modelling across the two families, superfamily-level homology justifies fold-level threading at best. Loop conformations, the calcium site and ligand-binding surfaces must not be copied from one family to the other.

6. EXTERNAL EVIDENCE STILL REQUIRED

To move from SCOPe's assertion to an independently defensible claim: read the primary reference PubMed 17977833 for the structural superposition and topology argument that drove the 2.05 move; run independent structure comparison (DALI or FATCAT) directly between d1nqda_ and d1dlca1, since neither appears in the other's SCOPe neighbour list; seek profile-HMM or HMM-HMM evidence (HHpred, Pfam) bridging the collagen-binding family to PF03944, which SCOPe does not supply because b.18.1.36 carries no Pfam cross-reference; and require direct binding assays before any functional statement, since function is not transferable at this evolutionary distance. Cross-checking CATH and ECOD placements of both domains would also test whether the superfamily merge is reproduced by other classification schemes.

Second, the comment cites the obsolete identifier d1nqdb_, which no longer resolves in 2.08; the curatorial note is stale with respect to current domain identifiers even though the classification itself is current.

(b) Topology and fold description. SCOPe describes b.18 Galactose-binding domain-like as "sandwich; 9 strands in 2 sheets; jelly-roll" and b.23 CUB-like as "sandwich, 10 strands in 2 sheets; jelly-roll". Both parent folds are jelly-roll beta sandwiches, which explains both the original 2.04 placement and why the correction is subtle rather than obvious: the discriminating feature is strand count and sheet topology, not overall architecture. The 1nqd PDB keywords themselves say "beta sandwich, metalloprotease, collagen-binding domain, calcium". The reassignment is a judgement that ColG CBD's strand topology matches the 9-stranded lectin-like galactose-binding/discoidin sandwich rather than the 10-stranded CUB sandwich.

(c) Structure-comparison evidence from SCOPe's own FATCAT-based neighbour lists. Querying chain 1nqdA returns an empty structure-hit list under the default filters (p <= 0.05, initial RMSD < 4), and the domain-level fatcat-chain-statistics for sunid 86025 returns status "not_applicable" with no supporting hits at the minimum of two. The informative list is for 1nqjA, the sequence-cluster representative of 1nqdA (99.16 percent identity over 119 alignment columns, Smith-Waterman). Its significant hits spread across the galactose-binding superfamily: d2quoa_ CPE C-terminal domain b.18.1.37 at p = 1.4e-06 and 10.26 percent identity; d2xh6a2 b.18.1.0 Clostridium perfringens automated match at p = 1.93e-06; d1wmfa1 alkaline serine protease KP-43 C-terminal domain b.18.1.20 at p = 2e-06; d1ux7a_ endo-1,4-beta-xylanase D b.18.1.28 at p = 1.32e-03; d2xhna3 b.18.1.0 at p = 2.17e-03. Independently, chain 1dlcA (its own cluster representative) hits d1w99a3 Cry4Ba delta-endotoxin C-terminal domain b.18.1.3 at p = 2e-04, d1ux7a_ b.18.1.28 at p = 7.46e-03 and d1w9wa_ CBM6 b.18.1.10 at p = 7.6e-03. Both domains therefore reach independently into b.18.1 at single-digit-to-low-double-digit sequence identity, and they share at least one common structural neighbour, xylanase D d1ux7a_. Crucially, neither hit list contains the other domain directly, so the structural support for the specific 1nqd-to-1dlc pair is transitive through superfamily members and not a direct pairwise FATCAT match. Residual CUB-like similarity persists too: 1nqjA still hits d3dema1 b.23.1.0 at p = 1.28e-03, which is why the original placement was defensible.

(d) Family membership consistency. Family b.18.1.36 now holds ten domains from five entries, all Clostridium histolyticum class I collagenase CBDs: d1nqda_, d1nqdb1, d1nqja_, d1nqjb_, d4hpka_, d4hpkb_, d2o8oa_, d2o8ob2, and the tandem pair d5ikua1 (A:773-890) and d5ikua2 (A:891-1008). Family b.18.1.3 holds the delta-endotoxin C-terminal domains including d1dlca1 and d1w99a3, and carries the comment "automatically mapped to Pfam 03944" with xref PF03944. The collagen-binding family has no Pfam cross-reference in 2.08, so sequence-profile corroboration is one-sided.

4. FUNCTIONAL EVIDENCE AND WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE

The shared functional logic is architectural, not mechanistic. Both domains are C-terminal accessory binding modules appended to a secreted multidomain bacterial virulence protein, each presenting a shallow face of a jelly-roll beta sandwich to a macromolecular target, and both sit in a superfamily dominated by targeting and ligand-binding modules: galactose-binding domain, discoidin/FA58C, CBM6, CBM15, CBM22, APC10-like, ephrin receptor ligand-binding domain, beta-galactosidase/glucuronidase N-terminal domain, XRCC1 N-terminal domain, KP-43 protease C-terminal domain. ColG CBD is the collagen-targeting module of the collagenase and is calcium dependent: 1nqd is the calcium-complexed form (domain comment "complexed with ca"), and the 2.04 superfamily annotation recorded that the "N-terminal strand appears only in calcium-free form". Cry3A domain III is the lectin-like C-terminal domain implicated in receptor and carbohydrate recognition and in specificity. Convergence on "substrate-adhesion module bolted onto a secreted toxin or enzyme" is consistent with descent from a common ligand-binding ancestor.

Unsafe transfers to avoid:

- Do not transfer binding specificity. The same scaffold in b.18.1 binds galactose, xylan, cellulose, ephrin, collagen and ubiquitin-ligase substrates. Superfamily membership says nothing about ligand. It is not supported to infer that Cry3A domain III binds collagen, nor that ColG CBD binds insect midgut receptors.
- Do not transfer catalytic or toxic function. Neither domain carries any activity. ColG's peptidase activity lies in its N-terminal M9B catalytic domain, which is absent from 1nqd entirely (the entry is only the isolated CBD 3B). Cry3A's membrane-perforating activity lies in domain I, classified separately as d1dlca3, sccs f.1.3.1, class f Membrane and cell surface proteins; 1dlc's middle lectin domain is d1dlca2 at b.77.2.1. So the homology statement touches only the accessory modules of both proteins and carries no implication about collagenolysis or insecticidal pore formation.
- Do not read family-level similarity into a superfamily-level claim. b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3 are distinct families precisely because sequence identity (about 10 to 26 percent in the relevant FATCAT comparisons) and functional divergence rule out a close relationship. SCOPe's homology_scope is "sf", not "fa".
- Do not treat the 2.04 and 2.08 records as interchangeable. Any pipeline keyed on sccs b.23.2.1 or on the domain identifier d1nqdb_ breaks silently against current SCOPe; a pipeline keyed on sunid 86025 still resolves but now means something different. Note also that sunid 86026 denoted whole-chain d1nqdb_ in 2.04 and denotes d1nqdb1 (B:893-1008) in 2.08, with residues B:891-892 split off as d1nqdb2 at l.1.1.1 (class l, artifacts). Domain boundaries were refined at the same time as the fold reassignment.

5. TEMPLATE AND REPRESENTATIVE CAVEATS

- 1nqd is the calcium-bound CBD; 1nqj is the related form and is the ASTRAL sequence-cluster representative for chain A. SCOPe's API explicitly warns that matches, coordinates and classifications of a representative must not be attributed directly to the requested chain, and the calcium-dependent N-terminal strand difference is a concrete reason that matters here. The structural evidence quoted above for ColG is representative-derived.
- Family b.18.1.36 mixes manual and automated assignments: d5ikua1 is an "automated match to d1nqda_". Choosing it as a modelling template inherits a propagated rather than curated classification.
- 1dlc is a 1994 deposition at 2.5 A with the SCOPe-selected PDB revision dated 2009-02-24, so it is a moderate-resolution template; Cry4Ba d1w99a3 is the family member actually used in the published homology argument.
- For modelling across the two families, superfamily-level homology justifies fold-level threading at best. Loop conformations, the calcium site and ligand-binding surfaces must not be copied from one family to the other.

6. EXTERNAL EVIDENCE STILL REQUIRED

To move from SCOPe's assertion to an independently defensible claim: read the primary reference PubMed 17977833 for the structural superposition and topology argument that drove the 2.05 move; run independent structure comparison (DALI or FATCAT) directly between d1nqda_ and d1dlca1, since neither appears in the other's SCOPe neighbour list; seek profile-HMM or HMM-HMM evidence (HHpred, Pfam) bridging the collagen-binding family to PF03944, which SCOPe does not supply because b.18.1.36 carries no Pfam cross-reference; and require direct binding assays before any functional statement, since function is not transferable at this evolutionary distance. Cross-checking CATH and ECOD placements of both domains would also test whether the superfamily merge is reproduced by other classification schemes.
